question: Before a 9 year old boy with testicular pain of 6 hours of evolution, intense, that almost prevents him from walking, without previous trauma, what is the most probable diagnosis?
analysis: The clinical presentation of acute, intense testicular pain in a 9-year-old boy, with a duration of 6 hours and no history of trauma, is highly suggestive of testicular torsion. Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency that typically presents with sudden onset of severe scrotal pain, often accompanied by nausea and vomiting. The absence of trauma and the age of the patient further support this diagnosis. While torsion of the appendix testis (Morgagni hydátide torsion) can also cause acute scrotal pain, it is usually less severe and the patient may still be able to walk. Epididymitis is less common in this age group and usually presents with more gradual onset of pain. A crural hernia is unlikely to present with isolated testicular pain.
